facts.fact: The World Bank's Additional Financing for the Social Protection and Economic Resilience Project (US$154.4m, estimated board date 28 May 2026) funds the legal and technical establishment of Mozambique's National Social Registry and its interoperability with civil registration, health and education data systems.
The same financing pays to modernise the core INAS management information system (eINAS) for interoperability with other government platforms; the date given is the document's own, 19 May 2026.

systems.owner: Ministry of Labor, Gender and Social Protection (DNPC, DNAS)

facts.fact: INGD's digital registry of humanitarian-assistance beneficiaries is being tested in Beira and is due nationwide in October 2026, and its director of prevention says it should interoperate with the INAS database to show who has already received assistance.

note: as_of is the article's published date; it gives no date for the pilot.

facts.fact: Mozambique's disaster agency INGD says its WFP-funded Beneficiary and Humanitarian Assistance Management System (SGBAH), in field pilot and validated ahead of an October 2026 national launch, will be interoperable with the database of the social action institute INAS, which runs support programmes for vulnerable households.

facts.fact: Mozambique's INGD says its digital register of humanitarian aid recipients, being tested in Beira and due to launch in October 2026 at a WFP-stated cost of about 20 million meticais, is to interoperate with the database of the social action institute INAS so the two show who has received food aid.
